terra.problem: Paul's role as an apostle and the letter's recipients are outside the passage and need references, such as Romans 1:1 and 1:7.
The statement that God cannot be seen goes beyond the passage's description of His invisible qualities and needs a reference.
The statement that God sends people with words is a Bible fact outside the passage and needs a reference.
The calendar comparison doesn't match the point: telling a boss when a report was due isn't claiming not to have known the deadline.
“The trouble came after that” adds a sequence the verse doesn't give. It says they knew God but did not glorify or thank Him.
“That's the point” assigns a purpose to the list that the text doesn't state.
The passage says God gave them over to impurity; it doesn't say He did not send a disaster.
The statement that God told Noah to build an ark needs its own reference, Genesis 6:14. Genesis 6:17 supports the flood statement.
“Creature” and “Creator” do not have the same letters.
The statement that Paul writes a lot about the law elsewhere in the letter needs a reference.
The statement that the Bible discusses testing elsewhere needs a reference.
“The mind leads to the actions” adds a causal explanation. The verse says God gave them up to a depraved mind to do what ought not to be done.
“Cheered others on” goes beyond the text's statement that they approved of those who practiced these things.
